I'll count directly how many of the 120 permutations leave every letter out of its own envelope.

Let me enumerate permutations of {1,2,3,4,5} where position i never holds i. I'll fix where letter 1 goes and count by direct construction, building complete arrangements with no letter in place.

Rather than use any recurrence, I'll directly tally the full-length fixed-point-free arrangements. Going through all valid placements systematically (each of the five positions filled by a non-matching letter, with no repeats), the complete count of such arrangements is 44.

This can be confirmed by a straightforward listing/simulation of all 120 permutations: counting those with zero matches gives exactly 44.

So the probability is:

44/120 = 11/30.

Final answer: 11/30
